M2 polarization of macrophages was found to upregulate glutamine catabolism, also known as glutaminolysis. In contrast to M1, M2 macrophages primarily rely on FAO and OXPHOS to fuel their functions [58]. Elevated FAO levels promote mitochondrial OXPHOS, ROS production, JAK1 phosphorylation, SHP1 dephosphorylation, ultimately resulting in STAT6 activation and the transcription of genes that regulate TAM generation and function [59]. While some studies highlight the predominance of FAO in M2 polarization, it is generally accepted that M2 macrophages retain a noticeable degree of glycolytic dependence and exhibit moderate glucose uptake.

Metabolic adaptations of TAMs not only supply them with energy but also directly influence their function by modulating transcription and post-transcriptional processes, impacting the composition of the secretome and thereby shaping specific immune responses during tumor progression. Importantly, tumor-specific metabolic alterations can occur in circulating monocytes before they infiltrate tissues, potentially predisposing them to pro-tumoral TAM programming during differentiation [46,47].
